facts.heading: Burnout since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burned out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October

facts.heading: Working three people's jobs
facts.content: Daniel ended up doing three people's jobs after his team was moved to a rescue plan.
facts.evidence: so I ended up doing three people's jobs

facts.heading: Working until 10pm
facts.content: Daniel answers messages at his desk until 10 at night.
facts.evidence: I'm still answering messages at ten at night

facts.heading: Sleeping four hours
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours

facts.heading: Waking at 3am
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at 3 in the morning and can't fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep

facts.heading: Thinking about work when not working
facts.content: Daniel thinks about work even when he is not working.
facts.evidence: Even when I'm not working I'm thinking about work

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn

facts.heading: Driving father to Leeds hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds

facts.heading: Sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto

facts.heading: Sister calls father every Sunday
facts.content: Daniel's sister Hannah calls their father every Sunday.
facts.evidence: She calls him every Sunday

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about being tired
facts.content: Daniel feels it is selfish to be tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill

facts.heading: Daniel hides his tiredness from Hannah
facts.content: Daniel tells Hannah he is fine when she asks how he is.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine

facts.heading: Daniel sits in car park
facts.content: Daniel sits in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before going in.
facts.evidence: I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before I go in

facts.heading: Claire booked Daniel's session
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend Claire booked his therapy session because she was done watching him disappear.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire.

facts.heading: Claire makes tea for Daniel
facts.content: Claire makes tea for Daniel and does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away for the weekend because he always says no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend, because I always say no.

facts.heading: Daniel runs ten kilometres every Saturday
facts.content: Daniel ran ten kilometres every Saturday morning for six years before October.
facts.evidence: Ten kilometres every Saturday morning. I'd done it for six years.

facts.heading: Daniel stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago because his legs felt like lead.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs felt like lead.

facts.heading: Daniel feels like he lost a part of himself
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself since he stopped running.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself.

facts.heading: Daniel answers Peterson's emails at night
facts.content: Daniel answers Peterson's emails at eleven at night even when he is in bed.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Daniel fears Peterson will let him go
facts.content: Daniel fears Peterson will let him go during the spring restructuring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Daniel has a mortgage
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage and feels horrible if he is relieved about losing his job.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week
facts.content: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week over nothing and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.
facts.evidence: I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing and went and sat in the toilets for ten minutes.

facts.heading: Daniel had heart attack symptoms
facts.content: Daniel had his heart going and hands shaking, thinking it was a heart attack, but it passed.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking. I thought for a second it was a heart attack, but it passed.

facts.heading: Daniel's GP said tests were normal
facts.content: Daniel's GP said blood tests were normal and attributed his state to stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests, and they were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion.

facts.heading: Daniel said he didn't have time to talk
facts.content: Daniel told his GP he hadn't got time to talk to someone.
facts.evidence: I said I hadn't got time.

facts.heading: Used train platform to stand
facts.content: Daniel stood on the train platform in Manchester.
facts.evidence: Once on the train to Manchester. I just had to get off and stand on the platform.

facts.heading: Hasn't told Claire about incident
facts.content: Daniel has not told Claire about the train incident.
facts.evidence: I haven't told anyone about it, not even Claire.

facts.heading: Afraid of losing coping
facts.content: Daniel fears he is losing his ability to cope.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Drinks six cups of coffee daily
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: Coffee, probably. I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Drinks two to three glasses of wine
facts.content: Daniel drinks two glasses of wine, sometimes three, in the evenings.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wakes at 3 AM after drinking wine
facts.content: Daniel wakes at 3 AM after drinking wine.
facts.evidence: It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Feels relief from talking
facts.content: Daniel feels a sense of relief from talking about his problems.
facts.evidence: Strange. A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Prioritizes sleep to cope
facts.content: Daniel believes sleeping would help him cope with the rest.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Identifies with grandfather's stoicism
facts.content: Daniel identifies with his grandfather's and father's stoic approach to life.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once. Dad's the same. You just get on with it.

facts.heading: Fears being seen as weak
facts.content: Daniel worries his grandfather would think he is weak for being in therapy.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Plans to stop phone use at 9:30 PM
facts.content: Daniel plans to stop using his phone at half past nine.
facts.evidence: Half past nine, perhaps.

facts.heading: Plans to have tea with Claire
facts.content: Daniel plans to have tea with Claire on the sofa.
facts.evidence: I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.heading: Plans to write a nightly note
facts.content: Daniel plans to write down when he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I'll write down when I wake up, if I wake up.

facts.heading: Feels lighter after talking
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after talking about his issues.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.
